independent_reference.source: Hand-derivation in tools/testkit/golden/derivations/d3q19.md §§ 1-5: Gauss-Hermite quadrature on the D3Q19 sub-lattice gives weights {1/3, 1/18, 1/36}, sound speed c_s² = 1/3, and the second-order equilibrium f_i^eq = w_i ρ (1 + c·u/c_s² + (c·u)²/(2 c_s⁴) - u²/(2 c_s²)). Every weight and velocity vector substituted directly from first principles; no upstream code consulted. Establishes the algebraic ground truth from which all subsequent anchors are cross-checked.

independent_reference.source: Qian, Y. H., d'Humières, D. & Lallemand, P. (1992), 'Lattice BGK Models for Navier-Stokes Equation', Europhysics Letters 17 (6), 479-484, DOI 10.1209/0295-5075/17/6/001, § 2 eq. (3a) plus Table 1 — the original D3Q19 specification. Weights w_i ∈ {1/3, 1/18, 1/36} per Table 1 row 3; equilibrium formula in eq. (3a) is the second-order Maxwell-Boltzmann truncation identical to this golden's algebraic form. Substituting (ρ=1, u=(0.1,0,0)) into eq. (3a) at each of the 19 velocity vectors reproduces the f_eq array above; the formula is published verbatim in the paper.
